conceptual assets.concept: Decompressed 32-bit instruction value produced by the decompressor
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements a combinational decompression: the process is sensitive to instr_i and builds a 32-bit decoded word (default `decoded <= x"00000003";` and many field writes such as `decoded(instr_opcode_msb_c downto instr_opcode_lsb_c) <= opcode_alui_c;`, `decoded(instr_imm12_msb_c downto instr_imm12_lsb_c) <= ...`, etc.). The entity then drives outputs from that internal word (`instr_o(31 downto 2) <= decoded(31 downto 2); instr_o(1) <= decoded(1) when (illegal = '0') else '0'; instr_o(0) <= decoded(0);`). These RTL facts establish that the correctness of the 32-bit instruction delivered on instr_o is defined by the module's decoding logic; incorrect modification of those computed fields would violate Integrity. Structural realization: instr_i is read to compute the value (sets), decoded is the internal storage of the computed 32-bit instruction (stores), and instr_o is the exit port through which the value leaves (exit port).

conceptual assets.concept: Illegal-instruction detection decision produced by the decompressor
conceptual assets.reasoning: The process computes an 'illegal' flag and uses it to alter the produced instruction: the RTL initializes `illegal <= '0';` and sets `illegal <= '1';` in several decoding branches (examples: in the "00"/"000" branch `if (instr_i(12 downto 5) = "00000000") then illegal <= '1'; end if;`, and other branches perform similar checks). The illegal signal directly gates output bit 1 (`instr_o(1) <= decoded(1) when (illegal = '0') else '0';`), so corruption or incorrect setting of this decision changes the delivered instruction and thus violates Integrity. Structural realization: instr_i is read to decide the flag (sets) and the internal signal illegal stores the decision (stores).
